title: Say what each inherited asset can't establish
statement: Before reusing an inherited bank, generator or source pack, record what each is useful for and what it cannot establish, since a high item score can hide a false source.
example: One course kept its 26,355 generated candidates for candidate prompts, distractor patterns and misconception mining, never for source clearance or certification.
detail: Reconciling an AP history course's local generation assets with the official framework found that generated candidates and legacy winners carried synthetic or weakly attributed source text, and that an item-level score can be high while its historical document is not reproducible or its attribution is false. The assets were not discarded but given narrower jobs, in a table of what each is useful for and what it cannot establish. The 26,355 generated candidates, for example, may supply candidate prompts, distractor patterns, misconception mining and repair starting points, never source clearance, current-format compliance, assessment independence or certification, and a label made by the same builder is not provenance evidence.

evidence.quote: The local APUSH assets are not discarded. They are assigned narrower jobs:
Generated candidates and legacy winners include synthetic or weakly attributed source text.
An item-level score can be high while its historical document is not reproducible or its attribution is false.

26,355 generated all-unit candidates, including 1,515 in Unit 1 | Candidate prompts, distractor patterns, misconception mining, and repair/top-up starting points | Source clearance, current-format compliance, assessment independence, or certification
A label generated by the same builder is not provenance evidence.
